lesson.theme: Telephone etiquette, health, requests, obligation, promises, causes, and formal intention
situations: asking to speak to another person
goals: Use -아/어 주다 and -아/어 주세요 for benefactive actions/requests
Recognize intentional -겠- and contrast it with conjectural -겠-

vocabulary.meaningEn: the line is busy; be on a call
to hang up; cut off; stop

grammar.name: Benefactive action
grammar.meaning: Adds the meaning of doing an action for someone's benefit.

examples.en: I bought bread for my friend.

contrast.note: Both can appear in requests, but -아/어 주세요 explicitly frames the requested action as a favor/benefit and the teacher presents it as more polite in this context.

commonMistakes: Do not translate 주다 literally as 'give' in every benefactive construction.

grammar.name: Obligation or necessity
grammar.meaning: Expresses having to/must do or be something; the teacher notes -아/어야 하다 sounds slightly more formal.

examples.en: I have to exercise every day.

examples.ko: 다음 학기에 한국어 수업을 들어야 돼요.
examples.en: I have to take Korean next semester.

grammar.name: Willingness, assurance, or promise
grammar.meaning: Expresses the speaker's willingness/assurance/promise, often with the listener in mind.
commonMistakes: The PPT restricts the subject to first person.
The PPT states -(으)ㄹ게요 cannot be used as a question.

contrast.note: -ㄹ래요 expresses/asks intention or preference; -ㄹ게요 presents willingness/assurance/promise and cannot be used as a question in this lesson.

grammar.name: Cause with a noun
grammar.meaning: Means 'because of N'; 때문에 must be preceded by a noun or noun phrase in this lesson.

examples.en: The road is congested because of the rain.
I was a little busy because of Korean class.

contrast.note: -아/어서 follows a verb/adjective clause; 때문에 follows a noun/noun phrase.

grammar.name: Intentional -겠-
grammar.meaning: Expresses the speaker's intention/volition in formal or courteous contexts and appears in fixed expressions.

examples.en: Thank you for the food / I will eat well.

contrast.note: Lesson 12 conjectural -겠- means 'I guess/it must be'; Lesson 13 intentional -겠- means 'I will' or marks courteous/formal willingness.

commonMistakes: The teacher notes intentional -겠- is not combined with past -았/었-.
In ordinary speech, -(으)ㄹ래요 may replace some intentional uses; courteous service/question forms such as 뭐 드시겠어요? remain important.

expressions.meaningEn: May I speak to OO? / Please put OO on the phone.
Take good care of yourself / Get well.

culture.title: Telephone etiquette and indirect politeness
culture.summary: The teacher's phone dialogues rely on conventional openings, identity checks, polite requests to transfer the call, and relationship-sensitive closings rather than face-to-face greetings.

practice.prompt: Which is the conventional telephone greeting?
practice.explanation: 여보세요 is the phone greeting taught in Lesson 13.

practice.prompt: You promise: 'I'll call you later.' Which ending fits?
practice.explanation: -(으)ㄹ게요 expresses first-person willingness/promise and is not a question in this lesson.

practice.prompt: Complete: 비 ___ 길이 막혀요. (because of the rain)
practice.explanation: N 때문에 follows a noun to express cause.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Please help me' as a benefactive request?
practice.explanation: 돕다 combines with -아/어 주다 as 도와 주다; 주세요 makes the request.
